DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with Superimposed Vascular Cognitive Impairment.

The combination of progressive leg weakness, unsteady gait, falls, bladder/bowel dysfunction (incontinence), and cognitive/behavioral changes (forgetfulness, paranoia) is highly suggestive of cervical spinal cord compression (myelopathy) causing central cord syndrome, potentially complicated by vascular dementia or normal pressure hydrocephalus. The MRI results are critical to confirm the level and severity of cord compression versus other intracranial pathology. Please ensure the MRI Cervical_Spine and MRI Brain reports are available for final confirmation.
